subChunks.title: TypeScript Integration
subChunks.hookHtml: Tailwind is CSS. TypeScript is JavaScript's type layer. Bridging them — typed variant props, typed token access, typed class strings — eliminates a category of bugs that plague large codebases: invalid variant names, missing required styles, and class strings that drift out of sync with component contracts.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Grand Archmage Solomon: "At scale, the cost of a misspelled variant name is not a missing class — it is a broken UI in production that no compiler caught. TypeScript with CVA catches it at the keyboard. That is the value."

VariantProps — typed CVA variants

import { cva, type VariantProps } from 'class-variance-authority';
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils';

const badgeVariants = cva(
  'inline-flex items-center rounded-full px-2.5 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium transition-colors',
  {
    variants: {
      variant: {
        default:     'bg-gray-100 text-gray-800',
        success:     'bg-emerald-100 text-emerald-800',
        warning:     'bg-amber-100 text-amber-800',
        error:       'bg-red-100 text-red-800',
        info:        'bg-blue-100 text-blue-800',
      },
      size: {
        sm: 'text-[10px] px-2 py-px',
        md: 'text-xs px-2.5 py-0.5',
        lg: 'text-sm px-3 py-1',
      },
    },
    defaultVariants: { variant: 'default', size: 'md' },
  }
);

// VariantProps extracts the TypeScript type from the CVA definition
type BadgeProps = VariantProps<typeof badgeVariants> & {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  className?: string;
};

function Badge({ variant, size, className, children }: BadgeProps) {
  return (
    <span className={cn(badgeVariants({ variant, size }), className)}>
      {children}
    </span>
  );
}

// TypeScript errors on invalid variants:
<Badge variant="sucess">...</Badge>   // ❌ Typo caught at compile time
<Badge variant="success">...</Badge>  // ✅

satisfies — type-safe class maps

// Without satisfies: TypeScript can't narrow the key type
const statusClasses = {
  active:   'bg-emerald-100 text-emerald-800',
  inactive: 'bg-gray-100 text-gray-700',
  error:    'bg-red-100 text-red-800',
};

// With satisfies: the map is type-checked against a record shape
type Status = 'active' | 'inactive' | 'error';

const statusClasses = {
  active:   'bg-emerald-100 text-emerald-800',
  inactive: 'bg-gray-100 text-gray-700',
  error:    'bg-red-100 text-red-800',
} satisfies Record<Status, string>;

// Now: statusClasses has literal string types, and the compiler
// ensures every Status has an entry.

Typed cn() with ClassValue

import { type ClassValue, clsx } from 'clsx';
import { twMerge } from 'tailwind-merge';

export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]): string {
  return twMerge(clsx(inputs));
}

// ClassValue accepts: string | string[] | Record<string, boolean> | undefined | null | false
// This gives callers maximum flexibility while maintaining type safety

Compound variants in CVA

const button = cva('inline-flex items-center font-medium rounded-md transition-colors', {
  variants: {
    variant:  { primary: 'bg-blue-600 text-white', ghost: 'text-gray-700' },
    size:     { sm: 'text-xs px-3 py-1.5', md: 'text-sm px-4 py-2' },
    disabled: { true: 'opacity-50 pointer-events-none', false: '' },
  },
  // Compound variants: apply classes when multiple conditions are true
  compoundVariants: [
    {
      variant: 'primary',
      disabled: false,
      class: 'hover:bg-blue-700 active:bg-blue-800',
    },
    {
      variant: 'ghost',
      disabled: false,
      class: 'hover:bg-gray-100',
    },
  ],
  defaultVariants: { variant: 'primary', size: 'md', disabled: false },
});

Extracting token types from @theme

// When using a token-based system, define the token names as a TypeScript union
type ColorToken = 'primary' | 'surface' | 'foreground' | 'muted';
type SpacingToken = 4 | 6 | 8 | 12 | 16 | 24;

// Type-safe token utility
function bgToken(token: ColorToken): string {
  return `bg-${token}`;
}

bgToken('primary')   // → 'bg-primary'  ✅
bgToken('purplee')   // ❌ TypeScript error

Solomon: "In a codebase with twenty engineers and five hundred components, VariantProps and satisfies prevent entire classes of production bugs. Types are not ceremony — they are documentation that the compiler enforces."

storyBeats.speaker: Grand Archmage Solomon
storyBeats.text: VariantProps extracts the TypeScript type from your CVA definition automatically. Your component's variant API is typed, IntelliSense shows all valid options, and a typo is a compile error — not a silent visual bug in production.

storyBeats.speaker: Typed badge with VariantProps

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a typed status display. In a real React component these would be typed, but in this HTML practice apply the correct classes to demonstrate the variant pattern:

  • .ts-badge: inline-flex, items-center, rounded-full, px-2.5, py-0.5, text-xs, font-medium
  • .ts-badge-success: bg-emerald-100, text-emerald-800
  • .ts-badge-warning: bg-amber-100, text-amber-800
  • .ts-badge-error: bg-red-100, text-red-800
  • .ts-badge-info: bg-blue-100, text-blue-800
  • .ts-btn: inline-flex, items-center, gap-2, font-medium, rounded-md, transition-colors, text-sm, px-4, py-2, bg-blue-600, text-white, hover:bg-blue-700
  • .ts-btn-ghost: inline-flex, items-center, gap-2, font-medium, rounded-md, transition-colors, text-sm, px-4, py-2, text-gray-700, hover:bg-gray-100

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a complete typed Input component in HTML/CSS that demonstrates three variants (default, error, success) and two sizes (sm, md). Write out the CVA definition as a comment block, then apply the resulting classes to three input examples. Include a compound variant that adds a ring when the input is both error and focused.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain what VariantProps<typeof buttonVariants> does in TypeScript. What type does it produce, and what specific class of bugs does it prevent? Also explain compound variants in CVA — when would you use one?

questions.prompt: What does VariantProps<typeof buttonVariants> produce in TypeScript?
options: A TypeScript type describing the valid variant and size props — e.g. { variant?: 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'ghost'; size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' }
The final CSS class string for the component
A runtime object mapping variant names to class strings
A generic type that must be manually specified — VariantProps is just a utility type placeholder
questions.answer: A TypeScript type describing the valid variant and size props — e.g. { variant?: 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'ghost'; size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' }
questions.explanation: VariantProps<typeof cvaFn> extracts the TypeScript interface from the CVA definition at the type level. It produces an object type where each variant key maps to a union of its valid values (marked optional since CVA has defaultVariants). This type is used as part of the component's props interface.

questions.prompt: A developer builds a status badge lookup: const classes = { active: 'bg-green-100 text-green-800', inactive: 'bg-gray-100 text-gray-700' }. New statuses are added regularly, and sometimes a status appears without a corresponding class. Which TypeScript pattern prevents missing entries?
options: satisfies Record<Status, string> — the compiler errors if any Status key is missing from the object
as const — narrows the type to literal strings
Readonly<Record<Status, string>> — prevents mutation but doesn't enforce completeness
Generic type parameter T extends string — allows any string key
questions.answer: satisfies Record<Status, string> — the compiler errors if any Status key is missing from the object
questions.explanation: satisfies verifies the object against Record<Status, string> at the type level without widening the inferred type. If Status = 'active' | 'inactive' | 'pending' and the object doesn't have a 'pending' key, TypeScript errors. as const only narrows existing values — it doesn't enforce exhaustiveness.

questions.prompt: When would you use a compound variant in CVA instead of a regular variant?
options: When a set of classes should only apply when multiple variant conditions are simultaneously true — e.g. hover classes only when variant=primary AND disabled=false
When you need more than 4 variant options — regular variants have a limit
When the same class applies to all variants — use a compound variant instead of the base string
Compound variants are the correct pattern for size variants; regular variants are for colour variants
questions.answer: When a set of classes should only apply when multiple variant conditions are simultaneously true — e.g. hover classes only when variant=primary AND disabled=false
questions.explanation: Compound variants solve the intersection problem: a disabled primary button shouldn't have hover styles, but hover:bg-blue-700 in the primary variant applies regardless of disabled state. A compound variant { variant: 'primary', disabled: false, class: 'hover:bg-blue-700' } applies the hover class only when both conditions are met.
